explain.say: Look at the Seeing group. Your eyes let you see. You see a rainbow, traffic lights and a friend's smile. Find 3 red things near you now.
Now look at the Hearing group. Your ears let you hear. You hear thunder, a doorbell and birdsong. You can hear them with your eyes shut. What is the quietest sound you can hear now?
Here are Smelling and Tasting. Your nose smells smoke, bread and jasmine flowers. Your tongue tastes lemon, salt and honey. Smell helps you to taste. Food tastes less strong when you have a cold.
Last, look at the skin. Skin is your sense of touch. It covers all of your body. It feels hot, cold, soft and sharp. Skin is your biggest organ. On a grown-up, it covers nearly 2 square metres.

faq.a: The five senses are sight with your eyes, hearing with your ears, smell with your nose, taste with your tongue and touch with your skin.

faq.q: Why can I not taste food when my nose is blocked?
faq.a: Much of what we call flavour actually comes from smell. When your nose is blocked, smells cannot reach it, so food tastes dull and your tongue only notices sweet, salty, sour, bitter and savoury.
asks: Why does food taste bland when I have a cold?

faq.q: What is the biggest sense organ?
faq.a: Your skin. It covers your whole body, about two square metres on an adult, and is full of tiny sensors for touch, pressure, heat, cold and pain.

faq.q: How do senses keep us safe?
faq.a: Senses warn us of danger: we smell smoke, hear a car horn, see a red light, taste food that has gone bad and feel a hot pan before we get badly hurt.

faq.q: What tastes can the tongue notice?
faq.a: The tongue notices five basic tastes: sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami, a savoury taste found in foods like tomatoes, cheese and soy sauce.

facts: An adult's skin covers about 1.5 to 2 square metres.
The tongue detects five basic tastes: sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami.

quiz.say: A doorbell rings. Which sense tells you?
quiz.show: 🔔 A doorbell rings. Which sense tells you?
quiz.why: Your ears pick up sounds. A doorbell is a sound, so you use hearing.

wrong.0: Sight uses your eyes. You can know the doorbell rang with your eyes shut.
wrong.2: Taste uses your tongue. It tells you about food.

quiz.say: You have a cold. Your nose is blocked. Why does food taste weaker?
quiz.show: 🤧 Blocked nose. Why does food taste weaker?
quiz.why: A lot of flavour comes from smell. With a blocked nose you smell less, so you taste less.

wrong.1: Your tongue still works. The smell is what is missing.
wrong.2: The food is the same. Your nose cannot smell it as well.
